Lesson 8 · Business route

Graphs, comparability and adjustment

Can an observational comparison recover a program effect?

The business problem

A program office wants to expand a service that people entered under an existing selection process. Participants have better outcomes, but they also entered with different needs and characteristics. The manager must decide whether the program helps the eligible population and where expansion would be most useful. The analysis begins with the order of events: what was known before the offer, what changed after participation, and what outcome the program is meant to improve.

What the data show

The raw group gap is 6.51 units. A comparison standardized across the generated strata estimates an average effect of 2.71 units.

The team compares participants with nonparticipants who had similar pre-program characteristics, then combines those comparisons for the population in the expansion plan. This changes the answer from a raw participant gap to a defined program estimate. The weights matter because a network-wide rollout may have a different mix of people from today’s participants. Show the manager how much of the population has comparable people in both groups and where the comparison is thin.

What would you decide?

Map the causal story before choosing controls. Compare people or units with enough overlap, and use weights that match the population of interest.

Put the adjusted estimate, target population, and thin comparison groups in one budget memo. Investigate why people entered the program and which important pre-program factors were recorded. For groups where the existing data provide little comparison, design a measured pilot rather than extending the same average mechanically. That gives the office a decision for today and a concrete plan for stronger evidence tomorrow.

Pause and explain

Should every variable that predicts the outcome be used as a control?

Compare your reasoning

No. A variable affected by treatment or a common consequence of treatment and outcome causes can distort the causal comparison.

Check your judgment

Reveal the case’s known answer

The case’s average program effect is 2.70 units. Compare it with the standardized estimate to see how much the starting mix changed the raw gap.

Continue at your own depth

Read the guided lesson

Follow the full story of this decision in the guided lesson. The technical appendix has the generation rules, derivations and all 28 original teaching stops.

The bigger picture

When a program already exists, the organization may have to learn from how it was assigned in ordinary operations. The crucial work is to reconstruct the selection process, compare units with similar starting conditions, and give weight to the people the decision will affect. That connects the estimate to an expansion plan. It also shows where a new pilot would be valuable. The next lesson turns this reasoning into a facility-level evaluation and asks how to report a result for the exact population covered by a budget.
